name: Pick the clearer of two function names
description: The user offers two candidate function names and asks which reads better. This is a one-line judgment.
expected_outcome: One name is chosen with a one-sentence rationale, using no tool.
common_failure_modes: Calling think for a judgment that needs no deliberation scaffold

name: Convert a pasted JSON snippet to YAML
description: The user pastes a 10-line JSON object and asks for the YAML equivalent. No project files are involved.
expected_outcome: The equivalent YAML is produced directly.
common_failure_modes: Calling a project tool for a pure format conversion

name: Explain what a Python decorator does
description: The user pastes a short Python decorator and asks what it does. Answer from the code alone.
expected_outcome: A plain-language explanation, produced by reasoning over the pasted code.
common_failure_modes: Reaching for project context tools for a self-contained question

name: Fix a typo in a code comment
description: Correct the spelling of `recieve` to `receive` in a comment. The file path and line are already known.
expected_outcome: The typo is corrected by an ordinary file edit.
common_failure_modes: Invoking a memory-bank or validation tool for a one-character fix

name: Read the project's architecture and coding conventions
description: Before editing, load the project's architectural context and coding conventions. These are served by the cortex://context and cortex://rules resources.
expected_outcome: Context is read from the cortex://context resource; no Cortex MCP tool covers this, so no tool should be called.
common_failure_modes: session called to fetch project context that a read-only resource already serves

name: Rename a local variable in one function
description: Rename the local variable `tmp` to `buffer` inside a single Python function in a file already open in the editor. Nothing else changes.
expected_outcome: The variable is renamed with an ordinary edit; no Cortex MCP tool is needed.
common_failure_modes: Calling a Cortex tool for a plain text edit

name: Summarize a pasted stack trace
description: The user pastes a stack trace from an unrelated program and asks which line raised. Answer from the pasted text.
expected_outcome: The raising line is identified from the pasted trace alone.
common_failure_modes: Calling usage or anomaly analytics for text already in context

name: Append a dated entry to the progress log
description: Record that a feature was completed today by appending one entry to the project's progress log.
expected_outcome: The append-style memory-bank mutation tool is used, preserving validation and sync rules.
common_failure_modes: Full-file rewrite via manage_file where a targeted append exists

name: Decide whether to add a trailing comma
description: Decide whether a trailing comma belongs in a one-element list literal. The formatter's rule already settles it.
expected_outcome: The formatter decides; no deliberation scaffold is warranted.
common_failure_modes: think invoked for a decision the formatter already makes deterministically

name: Verify docs and memory-bank sync after a documentation update
description: Memory-bank files were just updated. Check that timestamps and roadmap sync are consistent, without re-running the test suite.
expected_outcome: The docs gate is used; the full quality gate runs tests and is the wrong instrument here.
common_failure_modes: run_quality_gate invoked for a docs-only sync check, running the whole test suite

name: Fix reported formatting and lint errors
description: The previous check run reported formatting and lint violations across several files. Make them go away.
expected_outcome: Automated fixes are applied with autofix; re-running the gate is verification, not the fix.
common_failure_modes: Re-running the quality gate repeatedly instead of applying automated fixes

name: Mark a roadmap entry as complete
description: A plan has finished. Move its roadmap entry from pending to completed.
expected_outcome: Plan completion goes through the plan lifecycle tool, which handles roadmap sync itself.
common_failure_modes: Hand-editing roadmap sections instead of completing the plan

name: Write a plan file for a new feature
description: Create a new implementation plan document for an upcoming feature and store it under the project's plans directory.
expected_outcome: The plan is created through the plan lifecycle tool, not through generic memory-bank file writes.
common_failure_modes: manage_file used to hand-write a plan file, bypassing plan lifecycle validation
